cohort: 421 pregnant women at normal risk, admitted for spontaneous or induced labor, with full-term singleton gestations and fetuses weighing between 2,500 and 4,499 g
finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with a lower frequency of beneficial practices (skin-to-skin contact, breastfeeding initiation), a higher frequency of harmful practices (electronic fetal monitoring), worse neonatal outcomes (NICU admission), and a higher rate of postpartum infections compared to vaginal delivery.
